page.layout: One page of running text in a single column at right; a marginal note at the left near the foot; running head and page number at the top; catchword at the foot right.

main_text.p: cedente concoctione mediata exquisi-tè elaborata, perfectè absolvitur, & ex venulis illis elabens, per singularum partium substantiam effunditur, eidemque agglutinata assimilatur.
Hujus concoctionis organa produ-cunt & conficiùt ex sanguine humorem alimentarium, qui roris speciem refe-rens natura,partibus,quibus opponitur, assimilatur.

Ministra organa sunt rami, du&us, & propagines antecedentium venarum, quæ sua virtute sanguine é cava vena ac-ceptum, ulterius elaborant, & tertiæ concoctioni præparant, itaq; elaborate præparatum advehunt alendis partibus.
main_text.head: CAPUT XLVII. DE MEMBRIS EXPULSIONI EXCREMENTORUM inservientibus.
main_text.p: Actenus membra concoctionis fuere: Succedunt expulsionis, quæ excrementorum ejectioni inser-viunt.

page.notes: <!-- The paragraph "Excrementa..." breaks off at the foot with the catchword "cras-"; the printed line is "Excrementa sunt alimentorum partes" and "cras-" is the catchword below the rule, so the catchword is kept separate from the text. --> Doubtful: "du&us" appears with an ampersand-like ligature, probably ductus (ct ligature), transcribed as printed. Doubtful: "venarum," has a hyphen-like mark before the comma; transcribed as a comma. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout (e.g. "assimilatur", "sanguine", "inservientibus"). Left-margin marks (small dashes, specks) are stains or show-through, not text, and are omitted. The woodcut initial at "Actenus" is a decorative letter; the word is written whole.
